pages.text: MOWRAM information About the Ministry The Ministry of Water Resources and Meteorology serves as a staff member for the Royal Government of Cambodia on the leadership and management of the water resources and meteorology sector, including the work of the National Mekong Committee of Cambodia and the Tonle Sap Authority. This mission is carried out through the proper preparation and implementation of policies, legal frameworks and other legal documents related to the leadership and management of the water resources and meteorology sector, including the work of the National Mekong Committee of Cambodia and the River Authority. Sow. The Ministry of Water Resources and Meteorology has the following functions and duties: Establish policies and strategies for the development of water resources and meteorology for national, international business, development, and sustainable protection in accordance with the Royal Government's political program. • Study the water potential, including surface water, groundwater and air water in the national and international framework to establish a clear scientific and technical basis. • Set short-term, medium-term and long-term plans for doing business, developing and maintaining water resources to serve the national economy and livelihood of people in both urban and rural areas. • Manage and control all direct and indirect exploitation of water resources rationally and minimize potential disasters. Prepare laws, documents, norms and regulations related to water resources management and meteorology, as well as monitor implementation Compile, document and exploit meteorological and hydrological data to serve relevant national and international sectors for the benefit of society as a whole • Provide necessary technical support and guidance to the private sector, professional organizations, communities and the general public involved in improving and exploiting water resources appropriately. Expand and integrate modern technology to include training measures to improve and disseminate • Strengthen and expand national cooperation and international cooperation and meteorology. Participate in the implementation of work related to the Mekong River Basin in accordance with the duties of the Ministry.

pages.text: Privacy Policy Privacy Policy MOWRAM Human Resource Management System (HRMS) Data Controller: Ministry of Water Resources and Meteorology (MOWRAM), Kingdom of Cambodia Address: Contact for privacy matters: info@mowram.gov.kh Version: 1.1.1 Effective date: 15 August 2026 1. Introduction This Privacy Policy explains how MOWRAM collects, uses, stores, shares and protects personal data within the MOWRAM Human Resource Management System ("HRMS", "the System"), including its web application and mobile application. The HRMS is an internal administrative system used to manage the employment records of MOWRAM civil servants, contract staff, interns and other personnel ("Users", "you"). It is not a public service and is not open to general public registration. By using the HRMS you are acting in your capacity as a MOWRAM employee or authorised user. Use of the System is subject to this Policy and to MOWRAM’s internal IT and personnel regulations. 2. Who is responsible for your data MOWRAM is the data controller and owner of all personal data held in the HRMS. The System was developed and is maintained by MISTEAMS, which acts as a data processor on MOWRAM’s instructions under a written service agreement. The processor may not use HRMS data for its own purposes. 3. Personal data we collect Depending on your role and the modules enabled, the HRMS may process: a) Identity and contact data Full name in Khmer and Latin script, sex, date and place of birth, nationality, national identity card number, passport number, family book / residence details, photograph, home address, personal and official phone numbers, personal and official email addresses. b) Employment and civil-service data Employee/civil servant ID number, framework and rank, grade and step, position and job title, department or unit, duty station, date of appointment, contract type and dates, promotion, transfer, secondment and retirement records, employment history. c) Education and qualification data Diplomas, degrees, certificates, training courses attended, language and technical skills, professional licences. d) Attendance and time data Check-in and check-out records, working hours, overtime, mission and travel records, and — where the mobile app is used for attendance — GPS location and device information at the moment of check-in. e) Biometric authentication The mobile app may use your device’s built-in fingerprint or face unlock to confirm your identity when you sign in. This check is carried out entirely by your device’s own operating system. MOWRAM does not collect, receive, transmit or store any fingerprint, facial image or biometric template. No biometric data ever leaves your device, and the app itself has no access to it. The app is only told whether the device confirmed your identity or not. You can disable biometric sign-in at any time in your device settings and use your password instead. f) Leave and absence data Annual leave, sick leave, maternity and paternity leave, special leave, and supporting documents such as medical certificates. Health information contained in such documents is treated as sensitive data and is accessible only to authorised HR staff. g) Payroll and financial data Salary, allowances, bonuses, deductions, bank account number and bank name, tax identification number, National Social Security Fund (NSSF) number, pension contributions. h) Performance and disciplinary data Performance appraisals, objectives, evaluation scores, commendations, warnings, disciplinary proceedings and outcomes. i) Family and emergency data Marital status, spouse and dependent children (name, date of birth) for allowance purposes, and emergency contact details. Where you provide data about another person, you confirm they are aware you have done so. j) System and technical data Username, hashed password, role and permission assignments, IP address, browser or device type, operating system, app version, session times, and audit logs of actions taken in the System (records created, viewed, modified, approved or deleted). We do not collect data on your political opinions, religious beliefs, trade union membership or sexual life, and you should not enter such information into free-text fields. 4. How we collect data Directly from you, when you register, complete your profile, submit a leave or mission request, or upload a document. From MOWRAM HR and administrative departments, from your personnel file and official appointment documents. Automatically from the System, through attendance devices, mobile app usage and audit logging. From other government institutions where required by law, for example the Ministry of Civil Service, the Ministry of Economy and Finance, or the NSSF. 5. Why we use your data, and on what basis Purpose Basis Maintaining official personnel records of MOWRAM staff Performance of MOWRAM’s statutory functions as a public authority and employer under the Law on Common Statutes for Civil Servants Calculating and paying salary, allowances and deductions Legal obligation and performance of the employment relationship Recording attendance, leave, missions and working time Legal obligation and legitimate administration of the Ministry Managing recruitment, promotion, transfer, training and retirement Statutory functions Tax, pension and social security reporting Legal obligation Performance evaluation and disciplinary procedures Statutory functions Producing anonymous or aggregated statistics and workforce planning reports Legitimate administration; no individual is identified System security, audit, fraud prevention and investigation of misuse Legitimate interest of MOWRAM in protecting state information systems Responding to lawful requests from courts, auditors or competent authorities Legal obligation We do not use your data for marketing, advertising, or automated decision-making that produces legal effects on you without human review. 6. Who can see your data Access inside MOWRAM is granted on a strict need-to-know basis through role-based access control: You can view and, where permitted, edit your own profile. Your line manager can view attendance, leave and performance data of staff reporting to them. HR Department staff can access the personnel records necessary for their duties. Payroll and Finance staff can access payroll and bank data only. System administrators have technical access for maintenance, subject to logging and confidentiality undertakings. We may disclose data outside MOWRAM only where necessary and lawful, to: The Ministry of Civil Service / Secretariat of State for Civil Service, for civil servant registry purposes; The Ministry of Economy and Finance and the National Treasury, for payroll execution; The General Department of Taxation and the National Social Security Fund; The National Audit Authority, Anti-Corruption Unit, courts, or other competent authorities acting under legal powers; The System’s IT service provider, strictly for hosting, maintenance and support, under a confidentiality and data-processing agreement. We do not sell, rent or trade personal data. We do not share it with commercial third parties for their own purposes. 7. Where data is stored HRMS data is hosted on servers located at the MOWRAM data centre in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. All HRMS data is stored within the Kingdom of Cambodia. 8. How long we keep it Active personnel records: for the duration of your employment with MOWRAM. Records after departure, retirement or termination: retained in accordance with civil service archiving rules and the Law on Archives, as these records may be needed for pension, verification and historical purposes. When a retention period ends, data is securely deleted or irreversibly anonymised. 9. How we protect your data Measures in place include: Encryption of data in transit (HTTPS/TLS) and encryption at rest for sensitive fields; Passwords stored only as salted hashes; enforced password complexity; Role-based access control and the principle of least privilege; Full audit logging of access to and modification of personnel records; Regular backups, stored securely and tested for restoration; Physical security controls at the hosting location; Confidentiality obligations for all staff and contractors with access; Periodic security review, patching and vulnerability testing. No system can be guaranteed completely secure. You must keep your credentials confidential and must not share your account. Report any suspected compromise immediately to the MOWRAM IT Department at info@mowram.gov.kh . 10. Data breaches If a security incident affects your personal data and may cause harm, MOWRAM will investigate, contain the incident, and notify affected individuals and the competent authority (including the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications, once the Law on Personal Data Protection is in force) in line with applicable requirements, in principle within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach. 11. Your rights Subject to Cambodian law and to MOWRAM’s obligations as a public authority, you may: Access the personal data held about you in the HRMS; Request correction of data that is inaccurate or out of date; Request deletion of data that is no longer necessary and that we are not required to retain; Object to or request restriction of a specific processing activity; Withdraw consent where processing is based on your consent (for example, use of your photograph in an internal directory) — this does not affect processing required by law; Receive a copy of data you provided, in a common electronic format; Complain to MOWRAM, and to the competent regulator once established. Most corrections can be made directly in your profile or by request to the HR Department. For other requests, contact info@mowram.gov.kh . We will respond within 30 days of receiving your request. We may need to verify your identity first. Note that we cannot delete records we are legally required to maintain, such as payroll, tax and civil-service registry records. Account and data deletion requests To request deletion of your HRMS account and associated data, email info@mowram.gov.kh with the subject line "HRMS Data Deletion Request", stating your full name and employee ID. We will confirm receipt and explain which data can be deleted and which must be retained under Cambodian law. 12. Mobile application The HRMS mobile app is used by MOWRAM staff to record attendance and to view and submit HR requests. It requests the following device permissions: Camera — to scan the QR code displayed at your authorised duty station when you check in and check out. The camera image is read on your device to decode the QR code only. No photograph is taken, stored or sent to MOWRAM. Location (GPS) — to confirm that your check-in or check-out is taking place at an authorised MOWRAM site. Location is recorded only at the moment you press check-in or check-out. The app does not track your location in the background, and does not record your location at any other time. Fingerprint / face unlock (biometric) — to let you sign in using your device’s own security. See section 3(e); no biometric data is collected by MOWRAM. You can refuse or revoke these permissions in your device settings. If you refuse the camera or location permission, attendance check-in through the app will not work. The app displays no advertising and does not use your data for advertising or marketing purposes. The app uses Google Firebase Crashlytics to collect anonymous crash reports and technical diagnostic information. This is used only to identify and fix faults in the app. It does not identify you personally and is not used for advertising. 13. Cookies and similar technologies The web application uses strictly necessary cookies to maintain your login session and protect against cross-site request forgery. These cannot be disabled without breaking the System. 14. Children The HRMS is not intended for use by persons under 18. Data about employees’ children is processed only for family allowance and benefit purposes and is provided by the employee. 15. Changes to this Policy We may update this Policy to reflect changes in the System, in MOWRAM procedures, or in Cambodian law — in particular once the Law on Personal Data Protection is promulgated. Material changes will be announced within the System and by internal notice. The effective date shown at the top of this Policy indicates the current version. 16. Contact Questions, requests or complaints regarding this Policy: IT Department, Ministry of Water Resources and Meteorology Email: info@mowram.gov.kh A Khmer-language version of this Policy is available on the Khmer-language version of this website at mowram.gov.kh. In case of discrepancy, the Khmer version prevails. ឯកឧត្តមរដ្ឋមន្ត្រី ថោ ជេដ្ឋា អញ្ជើញជាអធិបតីបើកកិច្ចសន្ទនាស្តីពីអភិបាលកិច្ចទឹកនៅកម្ពុជា ឆ្នាំ២០២៦ ក្រោមប្រធានបទ«ការពង្រឹងអភិបាលកិច្ចទឹកនៅថ្នាក់ក្រោមជាតិ» >> ឯកឧត្តម អឿង ចន្ថា អនុរដ្ឋលេខាធិការ អញ្ជើញជាអធិបតីបើកវគ្គបណ្តុះបណ្តាលស្តីពី «ការគ្រប់គ្រងប្រព័ន្ធទិន្នន័យព័ត៌មានទឹក ការធ្វើមូ៉ដែល និងការប្រើប្រាស់រូបភាពផ្កាយរណប» ដើម្បីពង្រឹងសមត្ថភាពមន្ត្រីជំនាញ >> ឯកឧត្ដមរដ្ឋមន្ត្រី ថោ ជេដ្ឋា អញ្ជើញដឹកនាំគណៈប្រតិភូក្រសួងចូលរួមក្នុងព្រះរាជពិធីពន្លត់ភ្លើងជ័យ ក្រោមព្រះរាជាអធិបតីភាពដ៏ខ្ពង់ខ្ពស់បំផុត ព្រះករុណាព្រះបាទសម្តេចព្រះបរមនាថ នរោត្ដម សីហមុនី ព្រះមហាក្សត្រ នៃព្រះរាជាណាចក្រកម្ពុជា >> ឯកឧត្តម ពេជ្រ វាសនា អនុរដ្ឋលេខាធិការ អញ្ជើញអមដំណើរក្រុមបេសកកម្ម JICA ចុះពិនិត្យទីតាំងគម្រោងគ្រប់គ្រងទឹកជំនន់ស្ទឹងព្រែកត្នោត ស្ថិតក្នុងភូមិសាស្ដ្រខេត្តកំពង់ស្ពឺ >> ឯកឧត្តម ចាន់ យុត្ថា រដ្ឋលេខាធិការ អញ្ជើញដឹកនាំកិច្ចប្រជុំពិភាក្សាបញ្ចប់លើការរៀបចំសេចក្តីព្រាងអនុក្រឹត្យស្តីពី ការរៀបចំ និងការប្រព្រឹត្តទៅរបស់ក្រសួងធនធានទឹក និងឧតុនិយម

pages.title: HE Sot Raksmey, Secretary of State of the Ministry of Water Resources and Meteorology, inspected the water level in Stung Treng Province. - MOWRAM
pages.text: Posted on: 06-09-2023 | View: 2813 | Share =========== On Tuesday, the 5th day of the month of Srap, in the year of Thao, Panchasak, B.C. On September 5, 2023, Meteorology and Chairman of the Water Resources and Meteorology Coordination Working Group in Kratie and Stung Treng Provinces, accompanied by HE Run To, Under Meteorology. The director of the department and his colleagues province. During the inspection, the Secretary of State, accompanied by the Undersecretary of State and the Director of the Provincial Department, inspected the water situation at the Lower Sesan 2 Dam in Stung Treng Province. According to the report of the director of the department, the water level in the Lower Sesan 2 Dam is 75.26 meters above sea level, which appears to be a bit high, but did not cause the water level in the Sesan River. The lower part encounters abnormal problems. The director of the department added that as of today, at the hydrological station of Stung Treng Provincial Department, the water level in the Sesan River is only 4.7 meters (height from the bottom of the river) compared to 2022. Still lower. On the other hand, according to the director of the department, the water level must be careful unless the water level in the Sesan River reaches 10.5 meters and the alert height is 11.5 meters. The director of the department confirmed that both the amount of water in the Lower Sesan 2 Dam and the water level in the Lower Sesan River have not been noted to affect the crops and homes of the people yet.

pages.title: HE Thor Chetha Inspects Water Condition and Irrigation System in Siem Reap and Kampong Thom Provinces - MOWRAM
pages.text: Posted on: 12-09-2023 | View: 2947 | Share On the morning of Saturday, September 9, 2023, HE accompanied by His Excellency the Permanent Secretary of State, Undersecretary of State, Director of the Cabinet, Director of the Department, and officials. Experts inspected the water condition and met with the community of farmers using water at Makak Irrigation System in Chi Kreng District, Siem Reap Province. On that occasion, the HE Minister and his team, with the participation of the Deputy Provincial Governor, Chi Kreng District Governor, and Commune Chief, after meeting with 35 people from three water user communities, including Makak community, Area 1 and Afterwards, HE Minister and his team inspected the Makak Dam water controller and inspected the potential of the reservoir area and irrigation system. Please be informed that the Makak Irrigation System has been continuously maintained and repaired by the community, the Department, and Meteorology. With the source of water flowing from the upper Chi Kreng River to the lower part of the Tonle Sap River, the Makak Irrigation System, which was built in 1973 in Makak Village, Kork Thlok Leu Commune, Chi Kreng District, Siem Reap Province, is able to irrigate a large amount of rice during the rainy season. 25,000 hectares of dry rice, 8,000 hectares, and mixed crops of 1,000 hectares, of which 2,061 families benefited from this irrigation system. The Minister instructed to continue to strengthen the existing water farmers 'communities and requested all water farmers' communities to continue to help maintain the existing achievements to be able to use in the long run. In the afternoon of the same day, the HE Minister also continued to inspect the water condition and the Tang Krasang irrigation system in Santuk district # Kampong Thom province. It should be noted that Tang Krasang Irrigation System, located in Santuk District, Kampong Thom Province, was built during the Pol Pot era and can store 25 million cubic meters of water and can irrigate 8,360 hectares of wet paddy and 2,150 hectares of dry paddy. Tang Krasang irrigation system has two parts: the reservoir section is located in Kbal Bei village, Tipor commune, and the canal system is located in four communes: Tipor commune, Tang Krasaing commune, Chrob commune, and Kor Koh commune.
